data.narrative:
Substrate is a Series A-stage semiconductor company founded by James Proud and Oliver Proud that has raised $100M+. The valuation analysis draws on a universe of 11 peers across Chips & Semiconductors—3 public comps (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private-stage companies including SambaNova Systems, Cerebras, and Credo Semiconductor.

The Stage-Progression method is the primary applicable triangulation approach. Using the $100M total raised as a proxy for post-money valuation and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A to subsequent-stage progression yields an implied valuation of $200M. A Peer-Median approach was not feasible; while 12 same-sector peers exist, the narrow filters (same-stage, adjacent-stage, similar-valuation-tier) returned insufficient datapoints for statistical reliability. Public-Comp Anchoring could not be applied because Substrate's revenue is not on file, which is standard for private companies; the public semiconductor P/S median stands at 21.5x across the 3 tickers, but lacks an applicable denominator.

The triangulation supports a range of $170M to $230M, with a median of $200M. The analysis rests on a single method and carries material uncertainty around the appropriateness of the 2.0x multiplier for this particular company and stage transition. Revenue disclosure or additional private comparables at identical development stage would materially strengthen confidence in this range.
